::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 26th 1877  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection C0171: Box 29
:::

My dear [Miss Kekewich](people/person_806.qmd)

I am afraid I do not know of any such governess myself at present. The only one I do know of as free, is too young to be sent to the sea with young girls, and she  has not passed the examinations though I hope she will try

I think that you will see in the March [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) the address of a [Miss Kennedy](people/person_2307.qmd) at Cambridge who might be good to write to, and I have asked [Miss Keary](people/person_793.qmd) (the author of [the York and Lancaster Rose](other_books/otherbook_867.qmd)) to write to you if she knows of anything likely to be of use to you.

I am afraid that at present the graduates are girl-graduates![^2] 

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^2]: Alfred Tennyson, *The Princess* (1847) 141.  ‘Sweet girl graduates in their golden hair’.

**Note:** Trehawke Kekewich (1823-1909) of Peamore, Devon, was married, first, to Charlotte Peard (d. 1879), sister of CMY's friend the novelist Frances Mary Peard.  This letter was perhaps addressed to Alice Agatha Kekewich, later Carr (d. 1919), the eldest of his four daughters, or to another member of the family. The request was evidently for a recommendation of a governess who could coach girls for the Cambridge Local Examinations, which is the subject of the note in *MP* (March 1877), 288, referred to.
